neighbours.label: The noun naming the means or channel right after 'via', 'by' or 'through' (via email, by delivery, through cultivation), vs the same nouns used as subjects or objects
fire: Tickets can be booked via telephone or at the box office.
The documents were sent by courier the next morning.
The village is reachable only via ferry in winter.
Most of the water is lost through evaporation in summer.
Results will be shared via text once the lab is done.
The disease spreads through contact with infected animals.
Payments are accepted by cheque or bank transfer.
The data were collected through interviews with farmers.
quiet: The telephone in the box office rang all morning.
The courier left the documents at the wrong house.
The ferry to the village is cold in winter.
Evaporation is fastest on hot, windy days.
The text of the report was long and dull.
Contact with the farmers was friendly and easy.
The cheque was signed and put in an envelope.
The interviews with farmers took two weeks.

predictions: 'via/by/through <noun>' 0.3-0.8 on the noun; the same nouns as plain subjects or objects under 0.1.
notes: Card: scattered nouns after through/via/by/with (disorder, email, processing, cultivation, methods, delivery, Phone Call). Probe: 'via email' 0.799, 'by delivery' 0.548, 'through cultivation' 0.316, 'by genetic methods' 0.135 (adjective in between); 'The cultivation of rice' 0.018, 'Genetic methods are' 0.052, 'through the night' 0.015, 'for free' 0.155. Fire items put the noun right after the preposition.
